# Strings and memory

C's `<string.h>`: byte-string and raw memory operations.

<h2 id="memchr"><code>memchr</code></h2>

```rux
pub extern func memchr(
    ptr: *opaque,
    ch: c_int,
    count: size_t
) -> *opaque
```

Finds the first byte equal to `ch` within the first `count` bytes.
`ptr` is borrowed for the call and `count` bytes of it are read. `ch` is converted to an `unsigned char`
before comparison, so only its low eight bits matter. Returns a pointer into `ptr`, valid for as long as
`ptr` is, or null when no byte matches.
Runs in time proportional to `count` and allocates nothing.
`ptr` must be readable for `count` bytes. A `count` larger than the object reads past it.

**See also**: [https://en.cppreference.com/c/string/byte/memchr](https://en.cppreference.com/c/string/byte/memchr)

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/C/Src/String.rux#L42)

**Parameters**

| Name    | Type      | Description                                                                                   |
| ------- | --------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `ptr`   | `*opaque` | the block to act on                                                                           |
| `ch`    | `c_int`   | the character, as an `int` holding an `unsigned char` value or [`EOF`](/docs/api/c/stdio#eof) |
| `count` | `size_t`  | how many bytes to search                                                                      |

**Returns**: the address of the first matching byte, or null

<h2 id="memcmp"><code>memcmp</code></h2>

```rux
pub extern func memcmp(
    lhs: *opaque,
    rhs: *opaque,
    count: size_t
) -> c_int
```

Compares the first `count` bytes of two objects.
Both are borrowed for the call. Returns a negative value when `lhs` orders first, zero when the two ranges
are identical, and a positive value otherwise; the magnitude means nothing. Bytes are compared as
`unsigned char`, so the result does not depend on whether plain `char` is signed.
Runs in time proportional to `count` and allocates nothing. Not constant-time: it stops at the first
difference, so it must not be used to compare secrets.
Both pointers must be readable for `count` bytes.

**See also**: [https://en.cppreference.com/c/string/byte/memcmp](https://en.cppreference.com/c/string/byte/memcmp)

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/C/Src/String.rux#L57)

**Parameters**

| Name    | Type      | Description               |
| ------- | --------- | ------------------------- |
| `lhs`   | `*opaque` | the left operand          |
| `rhs`   | `*opaque` | the right operand         |
| `count` | `size_t`  | how many bytes to compare |

**Returns**: negative, zero or positive as the first differing byte orders

<h2 id="memcpy"><code>memcpy</code></h2>

```rux
pub extern func memcpy(
    dest: *var opaque,
    src: *opaque,
    count: size_t
) -> *var opaque
```

Copies `count` bytes from `src` to `dest`.
`src` is borrowed and read; `dest` is borrowed and written. Returns `dest`. The two ranges must not overlap --
that is what [`memmove`](/docs/api/c/string#memmove) is for, and overlapping them here is undefined rather than merely unpredictable.
Runs in time proportional to `count` and allocates nothing.
`dest` must be writable for `count` bytes, `src` readable for `count`, and the two must not overlap.

**See also**: [https://en.cppreference.com/c/string/byte/memcpy](https://en.cppreference.com/c/string/byte/memcpy)

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/C/Src/String.rux#L70)

**Parameters**

| Name    | Type          | Description               |
| ------- | ------------- | ------------------------- |
| `dest`  | `*var opaque` | where the bytes go        |
| `src`   | `*opaque`     | where the bytes come from |
| `count` | `size_t`      | how many bytes to copy    |

**Returns**: `dest`

<h2 id="memmove"><code>memmove</code></h2>

```rux
pub extern func memmove(
    dest: *var opaque,
    src: *opaque,
    count: size_t
) -> *var opaque
```

Copies `count` bytes from `src` to `dest`, correctly even when the two overlap.
`src` is borrowed and read; `dest` is borrowed and written. Returns `dest`. Behaves as though the source were
copied to a temporary first, so sliding a range within one buffer works in either direction.
Runs in time proportional to `count` and allocates nothing.
`dest` must be writable for `count` bytes and `src` readable for `count`.

**See also**: [https://en.cppreference.com/c/string/byte/memmove](https://en.cppreference.com/c/string/byte/memmove)

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/C/Src/String.rux#L83)

**Parameters**

| Name    | Type          | Description               |
| ------- | ------------- | ------------------------- |
| `dest`  | `*var opaque` | where the bytes go        |
| `src`   | `*opaque`     | where the bytes come from |
| `count` | `size_t`      | how many bytes to move    |

**Returns**: `dest`

<h2 id="memset"><code>memset</code></h2>

```rux
pub extern func memset(
    dest: *var opaque,
    ch: c_int,
    count: size_t
) -> *var opaque
```

Writes `ch` to each of the first `count` bytes of `dest`.
`dest` is borrowed and written. `ch` is converted to an `unsigned char`, so only its low eight bits are
stored. Returns `dest`.
Runs in time proportional to `count` and allocates nothing.
`dest` must be writable for `count` bytes. This is not the call for clearing a secret: a compiler is entitled
to delete a write nothing reads back, and `Core::Zeroize` is the one that is not.

**See also**: [https://en.cppreference.com/c/string/byte/memset](https://en.cppreference.com/c/string/byte/memset)

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/C/Src/String.rux#L97)

**Parameters**

| Name    | Type          | Description                                                                                   |
| ------- | ------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `dest`  | `*var opaque` | where the bytes go                                                                            |
| `ch`    | `c_int`       | the character, as an `int` holding an `unsigned char` value or [`EOF`](/docs/api/c/stdio#eof) |
| `count` | `size_t`      | how many bytes to write                                                                       |

**Returns**: `dest`

<h2 id="strlen"><code>strlen</code></h2>

```rux
pub extern func strlen(str: *char8) -> size_t
```

The length of a byte string, not counting its terminator.
`str` is borrowed and read up to and including its first zero byte. Returns the count of bytes before it.
Runs in time proportional to the result and allocates nothing.
`str` must be non-null and must contain a zero byte. Without one this reads until it faults or wraps.

**See also**: [https://en.cppreference.com/c/string/byte/strlen](https://en.cppreference.com/c/string/byte/strlen)

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/C/Src/String.rux#L107)

**Parameters**

| Name  | Type     | Description                   |
| ----- | -------- | ----------------------------- |
| `str` | `*char8` | a null-terminated byte string |

**Returns**: how many bytes precede the terminator

<h2 id="strcmp"><code>strcmp</code></h2>

```rux
pub extern func strcmp(lhs: *char8, rhs: *char8) -> c_int
```

Compares two byte strings.
Both are borrowed and read to their terminators. Returns a negative value when `lhs` orders first, zero when
the two are equal, and a positive value otherwise. Bytes are compared as `unsigned char`.
Runs in time proportional to the shorter string and allocates nothing. Not constant-time.
Both must be non-null and terminated.

**See also**: [https://en.cppreference.com/c/string/byte/strcmp](https://en.cppreference.com/c/string/byte/strcmp)

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/C/Src/String.rux#L119)

**Parameters**

| Name  | Type     | Description       |
| ----- | -------- | ----------------- |
| `lhs` | `*char8` | the left operand  |
| `rhs` | `*char8` | the right operand |

**Returns**: negative, zero or positive as the first differing byte orders

<h2 id="strncmp"><code>strncmp</code></h2>

```rux
pub extern func strncmp(
    lhs: *char8,
    rhs: *char8,
    count: size_t
) -> c_int
```

Compares at most `count` bytes of two byte strings.
Both are borrowed. Stops at `count` bytes or at either terminator, whichever comes first. Returns the same
three-way answer [`strcmp`](/docs/api/c/string#strcmp) does.
Runs in time proportional to `count` and allocates nothing. Not constant-time.
Both must be readable until a terminator or `count` bytes, whichever comes first.

**See also**: [https://en.cppreference.com/c/string/byte/strncmp](https://en.cppreference.com/c/string/byte/strncmp)

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/C/Src/String.rux#L132)

**Parameters**

| Name    | Type     | Description                       |
| ------- | -------- | --------------------------------- |
| `lhs`   | `*char8` | the left operand                  |
| `rhs`   | `*char8` | the right operand                 |
| `count` | `size_t` | how many bytes to compare at most |

**Returns**: negative, zero or positive as the first differing byte orders

<h2 id="strcpy"><code>strcpy</code></h2>

```rux
pub extern func strcpy(
    dest: *var char8,
    src: *char8
) -> *var char8
```

Copies a byte string, terminator included.
`src` is borrowed and read to its terminator; `dest` is borrowed and written. Returns `dest`.
Runs in time proportional to the source length and allocates nothing.
`dest` must have room for the source's length plus one, which this call has no way to check and does not.
Getting that wrong is the classic buffer overrun; prefer [`memcpy`](/docs/api/c/string#memcpy) with a length the caller computed.

**See also**: [https://en.cppreference.com/c/string/byte/strcpy](https://en.cppreference.com/c/string/byte/strcpy)

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/C/Src/String.rux#L144)

**Parameters**

| Name   | Type         | Description               |
| ------ | ------------ | ------------------------- |
| `dest` | `*var char8` | where the bytes go        |
| `src`  | `*char8`     | where the bytes come from |

**Returns**: `dest`

<h2 id="strncpy"><code>strncpy</code></h2>

```rux
pub extern func strncpy(
    dest: *var char8,
    src: *char8,
    count: size_t
) -> *var char8
```

Copies at most `count` bytes of a byte string, padding with zeros.
`src` is borrowed; `dest` is borrowed and written. Returns `dest`. Writes exactly `count` bytes: shorter
sources are zero-padded to fill them.
Runs in time proportional to `count` and allocates nothing.
`dest` must be writable for `count` bytes. This does **not** terminate the result when the source is `count`
bytes or longer, which is the trap in its name: it is not a bounded [`strcpy`](/docs/api/c/string#strcpy).

**See also**: [https://en.cppreference.com/c/string/byte/strncpy](https://en.cppreference.com/c/string/byte/strncpy)

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/C/Src/String.rux#L158)

**Parameters**

| Name    | Type         | Description                                  |
| ------- | ------------ | -------------------------------------------- |
| `dest`  | `*var char8` | where the bytes go                           |
| `src`   | `*char8`     | where the bytes come from                    |
| `count` | `size_t`     | how many bytes to write, terminator included |

**Returns**: `dest`, which is not terminated when `src` filled the count

<h2 id="strcat"><code>strcat</code></h2>

```rux
pub extern func strcat(
    dest: *var char8,
    src: *char8
) -> *var char8
```

Appends a byte string to the end of another.
`src` is borrowed; `dest` is borrowed, read to its terminator, and then written from there. Returns `dest`.
Runs in time proportional to the sum of the two lengths, since it finds the destination's end first.
`dest` must be terminated and must have room for both lengths plus one. Repeated appending is quadratic and
is a common accident: each call walks the destination from its start.

**See also**: [https://en.cppreference.com/c/string/byte/strcat](https://en.cppreference.com/c/string/byte/strcat)

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/C/Src/String.rux#L170)

**Parameters**

| Name   | Type         | Description               |
| ------ | ------------ | ------------------------- |
| `dest` | `*var char8` | where the bytes go        |
| `src`  | `*char8`     | where the bytes come from |

**Returns**: `dest`

<h2 id="strncat"><code>strncat</code></h2>

```rux
pub extern func strncat(
    dest: *var char8,
    src: *char8,
    count: size_t
) -> *var char8
```

Appends at most `count` bytes of a byte string to the end of another.
`src` is borrowed; `dest` is borrowed and written. Returns `dest`. Always terminates the result, so it writes
up to `count + 1` bytes past the destination's existing end.
Runs in time proportional to the destination's length plus `count`.
`dest` must be terminated and must have room for its own length plus `count` plus one. `count` bounds what is
taken from the source, not the size of the destination.

**See also**: [https://en.cppreference.com/c/string/byte/strncat](https://en.cppreference.com/c/string/byte/strncat)

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/C/Src/String.rux#L184)

**Parameters**

| Name    | Type         | Description                               |
| ------- | ------------ | ----------------------------------------- |
| `dest`  | `*var char8` | where the bytes go                        |
| `src`   | `*char8`     | where the bytes come from                 |
| `count` | `size_t`     | how many bytes to take from `src` at most |

**Returns**: `dest`

<h2 id="strchr"><code>strchr</code></h2>

```rux
pub extern func strchr(str: *char8, ch: c_int) -> *char8
```

Finds the first occurrence of a byte in a byte string.
`str` is borrowed. `ch` is converted to a `char` before comparison, and a `ch` of zero finds the terminator
rather than failing. Returns a pointer into `str`, or null when the byte does not occur.
Runs in time proportional to the string's length and allocates nothing.
`str` must be non-null and terminated.

**See also**: [https://en.cppreference.com/c/string/byte/strchr](https://en.cppreference.com/c/string/byte/strchr)

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/C/Src/String.rux#L196)

**Parameters**

| Name  | Type     | Description                                                                                   |
| ----- | -------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `str` | `*char8` | a null-terminated byte string                                                                 |
| `ch`  | `c_int`  | the character, as an `int` holding an `unsigned char` value or [`EOF`](/docs/api/c/stdio#eof) |

**Returns**: the address of the first matching byte, or null; the terminator counts as a byte

<h2 id="strrchr"><code>strrchr</code></h2>

```rux
pub extern func strrchr(str: *char8, ch: c_int) -> *char8
```

Finds the last occurrence of a byte in a byte string.
`str` is borrowed. A `ch` of zero finds the terminator. Returns a pointer into `str`, or null when the byte
does not occur.
Runs in time proportional to the string's length and allocates nothing.
`str` must be non-null and terminated.

**See also**: [https://en.cppreference.com/c/string/byte/strrchr](https://en.cppreference.com/c/string/byte/strrchr)

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/C/Src/String.rux#L208)

**Parameters**

| Name  | Type     | Description                                                                                   |
| ----- | -------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `str` | `*char8` | a null-terminated byte string                                                                 |
| `ch`  | `c_int`  | the character, as an `int` holding an `unsigned char` value or [`EOF`](/docs/api/c/stdio#eof) |

**Returns**: the address of the last matching byte, or null

<h2 id="strstr"><code>strstr</code></h2>

```rux
pub extern func strstr(
    haystack: *char8,
    needle: *char8
) -> *char8
```

Finds the first occurrence of one byte string within another.
Both are borrowed. An empty needle matches at the start. Returns a pointer into `haystack`, or null when the
needle does not occur.
Complexity is unspecified by the standard and is quadratic in the worst case on common implementations.
Both must be non-null and terminated.

**See also**: [https://en.cppreference.com/c/string/byte/strstr](https://en.cppreference.com/c/string/byte/strstr)

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/C/Src/String.rux#L220)

**Parameters**

| Name       | Type     | Description               |
| ---------- | -------- | ------------------------- |
| `haystack` | `*char8` | the string to search      |
| `needle`   | `*char8` | the substring to look for |

**Returns**: the address where `needle` starts in `haystack`, or null

<h2 id="strspn"><code>strspn</code></h2>

```rux
pub extern func strspn(
    str: *char8,
    accept: *char8
) -> size_t
```

The length of the leading run of bytes drawn only from `accept`.
Both are borrowed. Returns the index of the first byte of `str` not present in `accept`, which is the
string's length when every byte is.
Runs in time proportional to the product of the two lengths on a naive implementation.
Both must be non-null and terminated.

**See also**: [https://en.cppreference.com/c/string/byte/strspn](https://en.cppreference.com/c/string/byte/strspn)

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/C/Src/String.rux#L232)

**Parameters**

| Name     | Type     | Description                   |
| -------- | -------- | ----------------------------- |
| `str`    | `*char8` | a null-terminated byte string |
| `accept` | `*char8` | the set of bytes to accept    |

**Returns**: how many leading bytes are all in `accept`

<h2 id="strcspn"><code>strcspn</code></h2>

```rux
pub extern func strcspn(
    str: *char8,
    reject: *char8
) -> size_t
```

The length of the leading run of bytes drawn from none of `reject`.
Both are borrowed. Returns the index of the first byte of `str` present in `reject`, which is the string's
length when none is.
Both must be non-null and terminated.

**See also**: [https://en.cppreference.com/c/string/byte/strcspn](https://en.cppreference.com/c/string/byte/strcspn)


<h2 id="strtok"><code>strtok</code></h2>

```rux
pub extern func strtok(
    str: *var char8,
    delimiters: *char8
) -> *char8
```

Splits a byte string into tokens separated by any byte of `delimiters`.
`str` is borrowed and **modified**: a terminator is written over each delimiter found. Pass the string on the
first call and null on each call after it to continue the same scan. Returns the next token, or null when
none is left.
The scan's position is kept in storage shared by the whole program, so two interleaved scans destroy each
other and no two threads may use this at once. The string must be writable, which rules out a literal.

**See also**: [https://en.cppreference.com/c/string/byte/strtok](https://en.cppreference.com/c/string/byte/strtok)

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/C/Src/String.rux#L300)

**Parameters**

| Name         | Type         | Description                           |
| ------------ | ------------ | ------------------------------------- |
| `str`        | `*var char8` | a null-terminated byte string         |
| `delimiters` | `*char8`     | the set of bytes that separate tokens |

**Returns**: the next token, or null; the position is kept in storage shared by the whole program
